focus.label: Impact clarity
focus.selected_reason: This call's report suggested it. Your mission across calls doesn't change.
focus.why_it_matters: A solution needs a clear purpose.

checklist: Only then move to the solution.
example_wording: What usually goes wrong when that happens?
How much of your week goes into dealing with it?
What does this stop you from focusing on?
lesson.good_looks_like: Stay with the problem long enough to understand one or more real consequences: lost revenue, time, effort, slow growth, stress or risk. Use the prospect's own words. Don't fill in a number or a feeling they haven't given you.
lesson.quick_idea: Good discovery is not about asking more questions. When a prospect tells you a problem, your job is not to prove at once that you can solve it. First understand what that problem is actually causing.
lesson.source: Owner's Sales Xray specification, 9 Oct 2026 · Coaching §3 and §5.6
lesson.title: Understand the impact before you present the solution
lesson.when_not: Don't keep asking impact questions once the consequence is clear and the prospect has given enough detail. Don't repeat a question they've answered or push after a clear no. The goal is clarity, not interrogation.
lesson.when_to_use: When the prospect raises a real problem and what it costs them is still unclear. Check what they have already told you first.
lesson.why_it_matters: The prospect already knows the problem. Until its cost is clear, your solution can feel useful but not necessary. Impact gives the buyer a reason to change, and it makes the value and price conversation easier later.

limitations: This coaching is about one call. It doesn't show a pattern or mastery.
It stays with this report and doesn't replace your mission across calls.
When no Dipak lesson fits this focus, the written lesson stands in.

mastery.explanation: Mastery means doing the skill well in real moments, more than once. Your reports don't count those moments yet, so no mastery level is shown. More calls are not the same as mastery.
